name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: The stiff-leg deadlift is a hip-hinge movement performed with the knees kept nearly fully extended throughout. Unlike the Romanian deadlift — which maintains a consistent slight knee bend — the stiff-leg deadlift allows the bar to travel to the floor, requiring greater lumbar flexion and placing an extreme stretch on the hamstrings. It delivers a powerful hamstring and erector spinae stimulus but demands significant flexibility and careful attention to spinal position.

execution.starting_position: Stand with the barbell on the floor in front of you, feet hip-width apart. Grip the bar with both hands just outside the legs.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a double overhand grip or mixed grip. Lifting straps are appropriate for heavier loads as grip will be a limiting factor at extreme hamstring stretch positions.
steps: Step 1: With knees nearly fully extended (a micro-bend only), hinge forward from the hips and grip the bar.
Step 2: Brace the core and maintain a neutral or slightly extended spine as you lift the bar from the floor to standing.
Step 3: To begin the descent: push the hips back and hinge forward, keeping the knees straight, allowing the bar to travel down the legs.
Step 4: Lower the bar toward or to the floor, allowing the lower back to round slightly at the extreme bottom position if flexibility demands it. The key is a controlled, progressive range.
Step 5: Return to standing by driving the hips forward.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Hold through the stretch. Exhale as you return to standing.
common_mistakes: Fully locking the knees (hyperextending) — a micro-bend protects the posterior joint
Losing control of the lower back rounding too early in the range (should occur only near the floor)
Rounding the upper back significantly, transferring excessive load to the spine
safety_considerations: This exercise is not appropriate for those with insufficient hamstring flexibility — the Romanian deadlift is a safer alternative
Use moderate loads — the extreme stretch position is mechanically disadvantaged and high-risk under heavy load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower the bar until hamstring flexibility limits further range or the bar touches the floor, whichever comes first while maintaining acceptable spinal position.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-1-1-0 — a slow controlled descent to maximize the hamstring stimulus
coaching_cues: Slight knee bend throughout — never lock the knees
Bar stays close to the legs on the way down
Feel the stretch — don't let the low back take over
